name: Maine
tagline: From Acadia's granite shore to the St. John Valley, by way of Katahdin and Moosehead.
intro: Maine's byways follow the Down East coast from Mount Desert Island to Calais, and run inland through the western mountains and lake country to Katahdin and the Acadian St. John Valley on the Canadian line. This chapter follows the Maine Scenic Byways Program of the Maine Department of Transportation, whose thirteen byways Visit Maine lists, seven of them also National Scenic Byways or an All-American Road. Several were first designated in 1971 by route number and later renamed, and the national St. John Valley/Fish River byway joins two older state byways into one.

members.name: Schoodic National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Twenty-nine miles from Hancock along US 1 and down Route 186 around the Schoodic Peninsula, past Winter Harbor and the lobstering coves to a shingled 1891 lighthouse at Prospect Harbor and the quiet side of Acadia.

members.name: Bold Coast National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 1 and its loops wander 147 miles from Milbridge to Calais, by the working harbors of Jonesport, through Machias, where townspeople captured a British sloop in 1775, and out to the striped lighthouse at West Quoddy Head.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Rangeley Lakes National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 17 climbs from Byron to the Height of Land, looking out over the Rangeley lakes, then drops to Oquossoc and Rangeley and follows Route 4 down to the stepped cascades of Smalls Falls on the Sandy River.

members.name: Old Canada Road National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 201 runs 78 miles from Solon to the border beside the Kennebec and Wyman Lake, past the rafting village of The Forks and the Attean Pond lookout above Jackman, on the old road between Maine and Quebec.

members.name: Katahdin Woods & Waters National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Baxter State Park's south gate the road runs 89 miles through Millinocket and up Route 11 beside the Penobscot to Patten, with Katahdin in view from Ash Hill, then out to Grand Lake Matagamon.
members.note: Shown on the map as Grindstone Scenic Byway.

members.name: St. John Valley Cultural Byway/Fish River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 161 and US 1 follow the St. John River from Allagash past Fort Kent's 1839 blockhouse to Hamlin, through Acadian towns where French is as common as English. Route 11 runs south past Eagle Lake to Portage.
members.note: Shown on the map as State Route 11.

members.name: Acadia All-American Road
members.blurb: Route 3 crosses from Trenton onto Mount Desert Island and through Bar Harbor, then joins Acadia's Park Loop Road, built between 1921 and 1958, for Sand Beach, Otter Point, Jordan Pond and the road up Cadillac Mountain.

members.name: Blackwoods Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 182 leaves Franklin for unorganized woodland, curving around Spring River Lake and Tunk Lake under Tunk and Catherine mountains before coming down to Cherryfield and its blueberry barrens by the Narraguagus River.

members.name: High Peaks Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 27 climbs from the old mill town of Kingfield up the Carrabassett valley past Sugarloaf, through Stratton and Eustis by Flagstaff Lake, and along Chain of Ponds to the border at Coburn Gore.
members.note: Shown on the map as State Route 27.

members.name: Moosehead Lake Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 15 leaves Greenville along Moosehead Lake to Rockwood, across the water from the 700-foot cliffs of Mount Kineo, then runs on through the woods to Jackman. A spur follows Lily Bay Road to Kokadjo.
members.note: Shown on the map as Seboomook Scenic Byway.

members.name: Grafton Notch Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 26 follows the Bear River up from Newry into Grafton Notch, the pass between Old Speck and Baldpate, where Screw Auger Falls drops through a granite gorge, then comes down to Upton and Lake Umbagog.

members.name: Million Dollar View Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A short run of US 1 through Weston, with roadside turnouts looking over hayfields and the Chiputneticook lakes into New Brunswick, and west to the far shape of Katahdin.

members.name: Pequawket Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 113 runs up the Saco valley from Standish to Fryeburg, where the Pequawket village once stood at a bend of the river, then north along and twice across the New Hampshire line toward Gilead.
